# positionR <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="138" alt="" />

[![License: GPL (>= 3)](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-GPL%20(%3E%3D%203)-blue.svg)](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0)

positionR is a suite of four R packages for studies that track aquatic animals with fixed
acoustic receivers. The tools span end-to-end functionality, including designing telemetry
arrays, simulating animal movements, loading and filtering datasets, and estimating animal
positions. The packages can generate data and integrate user data from telemetry studies. The **positionR** package installs all four and does not attach them; each can also be
installed on its own.

- **detqc** reads detection, tagging and receiver deployment files from OTN, GLATOS and
  InnovaSea, runs a range of data checks and filters, reviews mortality, and generates a
  processing report.
- **detfield** generates estimates of animal positions as a probability surface using patterns
  of detection, non-detection, and the associated detection range models.
- **arraydesign** assesses receiver array design coverage, simulates animal tracks and their
  detections, and scores how well a receiver array positions them.
- **arraydesignR** is arraydesign as a point-and-click app.

## Install

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("jakebrownscombe/positionR")
```

One package on its own:

```r
remotes::install_github("jakebrownscombe/detqc")
remotes::install_github("jakebrownscombe/detfield")
remotes::install_github("jakebrownscombe/arraydesign")
remotes::install_github("jakebrownscombe/arraydesignR")
```

`positionR_packages()` lists the four with the versions installed:

```{r packages}
positionR::positionR_packages()
```

## The suite

<img src="man/figures/concept_suite.png" width="100%" alt="The four positionR packages and their functions, from the user's files to the tools the results are exported to." />

*The functions of each package in the order of a study, from your files to the tools the results
go to.*

- [**detqc**](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detqc/): read, check and filter detections.

  <img src="man/figures/suite_detqc.png" width="70%" alt="Screenshot of the top of a detqc review card: the animal's band and candidate death date, and a map of the stations that heard it." />

  *The top of the review card of walleye ST-02 in the simulated Stoney Lake study, which the
  rules put in the dead band.*

  [Get started with **detqc**](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detqc/articles/detqc.html).

- [**detfield**](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detfield/): detection fields and positions.

  <img src="man/figures/suite_detfield.png" width="70%" alt="Map of one simulated animal's 12-hour track in Stoney Lake with each hour's estimated position joined to its mean true position." />

  *Hourly positions of simulated animal stoney-01 from 16:00 UTC on 1 June to 04:00 UTC on
  2 June 2024. Each hour's posterior mean is joined by its error to the animal's mean true
  position in that hour, and the true track has one position a minute. The hours heard by two
  receivers or more fall a median 93 m from the truth; the two single-receiver hours fall 114
  and 165 m from it. Each receiver's detections are counted over these 12 hours. All 8
  receivers in view heard the animal; the study has 70.*

  Get started: [Fish positioning with detection range
  information](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detfield/articles/detfield.html).

- [**arraydesign**](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/arraydesign/): design and test the
  performance of tracking systems.

  <img src="man/figures/suite_arraydesign.png" width="70%" alt="Detection probability over Stoney Lake under 20 receivers on a grid: high round each receiver, low over most of the lake." />

  ```{r coverage-count, include = FALSE}
  # Rebuild the field that the picture shows, so that the knit computes the
  # caption's count.
  lake <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "stoney_depth.tif", package = "arraydesign"))
  deployable <- terra::ifel(abs(lake) < 1, NA, lake)
  receivers <- arraydesign::place_receivers(deployable, n = 20, method = "grid", seed = 1)
  range_model <- detfield::de_logistic(d50 = c(250, 750), d05 = c(500, 1500), depth = c(1, 35))
  field <- suppressMessages(detfield::de_field(detfield::water_distances(lake, receivers),
                                               range_model))
  p_any <- 1 - apply(1 - field$p, 1, prod)
  n_receivers <- nrow(receivers)
  n_heard <- format(sum(p_any >= 0.5), big.mark = ",")
  n_water <- format(length(p_any), big.mark = ",")
  ```

  *Probability that one transmission from each 100 m water cell of Stoney Lake is heard by at
  least one of `r n_receivers` receivers. The receivers sit on a grid over water at least 1 m
  deep. The range model is a stand-in curve whose 50% distance is 250 m at a receiver 1 m deep
  and 750 m at one 35 m deep. In `r n_heard` of the `r n_water` water cells that probability is
  0.5 or more.*

  Get started: [Design and test an array for Stoney
  Lake](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/arraydesign/articles/arraydesign.html).

- [**arraydesignR**](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/arraydesignR/): **arraydesign** as a
  point-and-click application.

  <img src="man/figures/suite_arraydesignR.png" width="70%" alt="Screenshot of the arraydesignR Map tab: sidebar at left, coverage map of Stoney Lake at right." />

  *The Map tab of the application on the bundled Stoney Lake raster, at its default
  settings of 20 receivers on a grid. The receivers and the range model are those of the arraydesign picture
  above, so the app counts the same `r n_heard` water cells at 0.5 or more.*

  Get started: [The app, tab by
  tab](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/arraydesignR/articles/arraydesignR.html).

## Acoustic telemetry studies, end to end

1. **Design and test the array.** `place_receivers()` and `evaluate_array()` in
   **arraydesign**: [Design an array for your own water body: compare
   layouts](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/arraydesign/articles/design-an-array.html).
2. **Read, check and filter the detections.** `read_detections()`, `check_detset()`, the
   `filter_` functions and `review_mortality()` in **detqc**: [Base processing: read, check,
   and filter telemetry data](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detqc/articles/reading-files.html).
3. **Fit or bring a range model and build the field.** `range_test_counts()`, `de_model()`,
   `water_distances()` and `de_field()` in **detfield**: [Range models: bring your own, or
   start from two distances](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detfield/articles/range-model.html).
4. **Position the animals.** `as_detfield_input()` in **detqc**, then `bin_detections()`,
   `location_surface()` and `credible_region()` in **detfield**: [Position fish from a cleaned
   detection set](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detfield/articles/from-detqc.html).
5. **Export.** `write_detset()`, `to_glatos()` and `processing_report()` in **detqc**, and
   `sample_locations()` in **detfield**: [Export the dataset and generate a summary
   report](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detqc/articles/exporting.html).

Steps 2 to 4 on your own files, where `field` is the detection field of step 3:

```{r study, eval = FALSE}
library(detqc)
dets <- detset(read_detections("dets.csv"), read_deployments("receivers.csv"),
  read_animals("animals.csv", tag_specs = read_tag_specs("tags.csv")))
dets <- filter_min_lag(check_detset(dets), max_lag_s = 4500)
counts <- do.call(detfield::bin_detections, as_detfield_input(dets))
surface <- detfield::location_surface(counts, field)
```

## Coming from positionR 1.x

Version 2.0.0 of **positionR** starts a new line of packages. **positionR** 1.x was one
package that positioned animals by weighted average detection efficiency (WADE). The four
packages do not yet do everything it did. None of them estimates space use, draws absences
from a space-use region, weights receivers by information or analyses behavioural states. The
Stoney Lake walleye detections of 1.x are not included. Keep **positionR** `r v1_version` for
those jobs; the [changelog](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/positionR/news/index.html) maps
every 1.x function to its place in the four packages. For habitat selection, **detfield** draws
presence points from position surfaces and availability points from the array's detection
probability. It stacks them into the table a conditional logistic regression takes, and fits
no model. Its [habitat-selection
article](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detfield/articles/habitat-selection.html) shows
that position draws underestimate a preference for shallow water.

```{r v1-install, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cat("```r", sprintf('remotes::install_github("jakebrownscombe/positionR@%s")', v1_tag), "```",
    sep = "\n")
```
